title: One claim, two shapes, two different answers
lede: Simulated: the mock PingFederate mints the access token with isMemberOf shaped by the scenario. The mock policy door reads the claim the way the policy says (array membership or substring) and allows or refuses the MCP tool call.

nodes.label: Call refused
sub: the reason names the shape mismatch

steps.title: The token mint shapes the claim
steps.what: The mock PingFederate puts the user's MCPAccess groups into isMemberOf, shaped by the scenario: a delimited string, or a real JSON array.
steps.why: The shape is decided at the token mapping, before any policy runs. It is the one knob this whole use case turns.

steps.title: The policy reads the claim
steps.what: The door evaluates the policy (contains MCPAccess-Atlan-Read) against the claim: exact membership when it says array, a text search when it says substring.
steps.why: A policy written for an array can never match a string claim, and a policy that searches text matches decoy names too.
